English: Greetings, trespasser. I have been watching you for some time; trampling on my grounds, desecrating my home, erecting your petty trinkets.
Chinese: 你好啊,闯入者。我观察你有一阵子了;你践踏我的地盘,亵渎我的家,竖起你那些无聊的小玩意。

English: And I have watched you as you sleep. I have savoured your flesh; drunk from your blood; tasted your dreams.
Chinese: 我也看着你入睡。我品尝过你的血肉;啜饮过你的鲜血;回味过你的梦。

English: I thought you would flee in terror, but still you linger where you do not belong. So I ask you, trespasser - why do you torment me so?
Chinese: 我以为你会吓得逃走,但你偏偏还赖在你不属于的地方。所以我问你,闯入者——你为何如此折磨我?

English: ((I'm)) tormenting ((you?)) There's a monster in my basement!
Chinese: ((我))折磨((你?))我的地下室里有个怪物!

English: <<The creature releases a guttural sigh.>> Monster, indeed. It has been many a century since I could hold my own gaze in a mirror.
Chinese: <<那造物发出一声低沉的叹息。>>怪物,的确。已经许多个世纪,我不敢在镜中与自己对视了。

English: But monster or no, this is ((not)) your basement.
Chinese: 但怪物也好,不是也罢,这里((不是))你的地下室。

English: I'm no trespasser, I bought this house fair and square.
Chinese: 我不是什么闯入者,这房子是我光明正大买下的。

English: Oh? And what thief brokered this deal?
Chinese: 哦?那么是哪个贼促成的这笔交易?

English: Prepare to die, parasite.
Chinese: 准备去死吧,寄生虫。

English: Would you be so quick to slaughter another living, breathing soul? Listen but a moment, trespasser, before you draw your blade.
Chinese: 你就这么急着宰掉另一个活着的、呼吸着的灵魂吗?拔剑之前,听我说片刻,闯入者。

English: These grounds are my prison; but they are also my home. I saw these timbers raised some two hundred years ago and I have dwelled here ever since.
Chinese: 这片土地是我的监狱;但也是我的家。两百年前我看着这些梁木立起,自那以后我便一直住在这里。

English: You may have purchased a scrap of paper for a considerable sum. Perhaps it bears the signature of some foppish noble? I care not. These lands are mine.
Chinese: 你或许花了一大笔钱买下一张废纸。也许上面还有某个富得流油的贵族签名?我不在乎。这片土地是我的。

English: <<She takes a deep breath.>> ((But)). There are things more valuable than even a home. Such as one's ((freedom)).
Chinese: <<她深吸一口气。>>((但是)).有些东西比家更宝贵。比如一个人的((自由))。

English: I am shackled here, trespasser; held captive within my own grounds, by powerful cipher magic. If you would help me win my freedom, I would recognize your claim to this manor. ##What do you say?
Chinese: 我被锁在这里,闯入者;被强大的密文魔法囚禁在我自己的地盘之内。若你帮我赢得自由,我便承认你对这座庄园的所有权。##你觉得如何?

English: You attacked me while I slept! Why should I trust you?
Chinese: 你在我睡觉时袭击了我!我为什么要信你?

English: I admit we may have got off to a wrong start. But remember, trespasser, that you cast the first stone. It is natural to act rashly when threatened.
Chinese: 我承认我们也许开场不太愉快。但记住,闯入者,是你先动的手。受到威胁时行事鲁莽,乃人之常情。

English: Let's say I ((do)) help. Will you leave me alone?
Chinese: 就算我((帮))了你。你会放过我吗?

English: Alas, there are few places for a creature like me to live safely. If you grant me freedom, I would permit you governance of the manor, staying myself in these underhalls.
Chinese: 唉,像我这样的造物,能安全栖身的地方寥寥无几。若你赐我自由,我准许你掌管庄园,我自己则住在这些地下厅堂里。

English: But oh, what wonders freedom would bring! I would be much enriched by my travels, and would grant you great boons after feasting on your flesh.
Chinese: 但哦,自由会带来何等奇迹!我的游历将使我大为丰富,而我大啖你的血肉之后,会赐你丰厚的恩惠。

English: Hold on - you'd still drink my blood?
Chinese: 等等——你还是要喝我的血?

English: You really are a monster!
Chinese: 你果然是个怪物!

English: Oh, the kiss of a vierme is nothing so crude as merely ((sucking blood)). It is a tender union of two souls.
Chinese: 哦,维尔姆之吻可没这么粗鄙,不只是((吸血))而已。那是两个灵魂温柔的交融。

English: My worm-tongue bonds with your nervous system, and for a beautiful moment our minds are as one. The dreams you have seen? They are my own. A gift, in exchange for sustenance.
Chinese: 我的蠕舌与你的神经系统相连,在美好的片刻里,我们的心智合而为一。你看见的那些梦?那是我自己的。以梦为礼,换取养分。

English: With my freedom, in exchange for a portion of your [[Health]] - you would be [[invigorated]] after waking here. Your senses heightened; your reflexes sharpened.
Chinese: 换取我的自由,只需付出你的一部分[[生命]]——在此醒来后,你会[[神清气爽]].感官更敏锐,反应更迅捷。

English: Very well, I'll help.
Chinese: 好,我帮你。

English: Excellent. Here is what you must do.
Chinese: 太好了。你须如此行事。

English: In the forest of [[western Hallowshire]] there is a decrepit house, not dissimilar to my own. I once frequented that place; [[this key]] will unlock it.
Chinese: 在[[哈洛郡西部]]的森林里,有一座破败的屋子,与我这里并无二致。我曾常去那地方;[[这把钥匙]]可以打开它。

English: A vierme lived there, once; I do not know if they remain. But I know this; that they were captive like me, and cast off their oppressor. Recover their [[spellbook]] and I might do the same.
Chinese: 曾有一位维尔姆住在那里;我不知道它是否还在。但我知道这一点:它和我一样被囚,却摆脱了压迫者。取回它的[[咒法书]],我或许也能如法炮制。

English: Okay, but I have some questions first.
Chinese: 好吧,但我先有几个问题。

English: By all means.
Chinese: 请便。

English: I'll get going, then.
Chinese: 那我这就去。

English: Thank you, and good luck.
Chinese: 谢谢,祝你好运。

English: And what if I say no?
Chinese: 我要是说不呢?

English: Then I suppose we would settle this matter as animals, with tooth and claw. But beware, trespasser; my bite is more dangerous in your waking hours.
Chinese: 那么我想,我们就像野兽一样,用爪牙解决这件事。但当心,闯入者;你醒着的时候,我的咬噬更危险。

English: No deal, monster. Prepare to die.
Chinese: 没得谈,怪物。准备受死吧。

English: So be it. Savour these moments, trespasser, for they are your last.
Chinese: 那便如此。细细品味这些时刻吧,闯入者,因为这是你最后的时光。

English: You have returned.
Chinese: 你回来了。

English: It is good to see you again, my friend.
Chinese: 很高兴再见到你,我的朋友。

English: Tell me again how I can free you.
Chinese: 再跟我说一遍怎么才能解救你。

English: Where can I find that spellbook, again?
Chinese: 那本咒法书在哪儿来着?

English: I've brought the spellbook.
Chinese: 我把咒法书带来了。

English: I had worried it was lost. This is an exquisite gift, mortal.
Chinese: 我还担心它失传了。这是件精美的礼物,凡人。

English: <<The vierme flicks to a certain page of the book and tears it free. She speaks a flurry of cipher and the air turns cold. A sound reverberates in your mind like a thousand glasses smashing.>>
Chinese: <<维尔姆翻到书中某一页,将其撕下。她念出一串密文,空气骤然变冷。一个声音在你脑海中回荡,宛如千只玻璃杯同时碎裂。>>

English: Oh, I feel it already - a great weight has been lifted! ##I have my freedom, and you have my sincerest thanks.
Chinese: 哦,我已经感觉到了——一副千斤重担终于卸下!##我重获自由,你也得到我最诚挚的谢意。

English: I will fly through the skyrealms once more, to take in wonders and beauty both. The kiss of a free vierme is a wonderful thing, mortal; you will share in my euphoria when you wake in your bed.
Chinese: 我将再度翱翔于天空领域,饱览奇观与美景。自由维尔姆之吻是何等美妙,凡人;当你躺在床上醒来时,便会分享我的狂喜。

English: Uh... thanks.
Chinese: 呃……谢了。

English: My pleasure.
Chinese: 我的荣幸。

English: How does it feel to be free?
Chinese: 自由的感觉如何?

English: What sort of creature are you?
Chinese: 你是什么样的造物?

English: I am a vierme - named after the parasite that lives inside me. It hungers for more than just flesh. Human thoughts, feelings, emotions - these are its sustenance. And so my kind stalks through the night, feeding on dreams.
Chinese: 我是一名维尔姆——因寄居于我体内的寄生虫而得名。它渴求的不只是血肉。人类的思想、感受、情感——这些才是它的食粮。因此我的同类在夜里潜行,以梦为食。

English: I think I'm a vierme, too.
Chinese: 我想我也是维尔姆。

English: <<The vierme sniffs the air with a quizzical look.>> Ah,  yes; I can smell it now. Very faint; you must have been infected recently...
Chinese: <<维尔姆满脸狐疑地嗅了嗅空气。>>啊,对;我现在闻到了。非常淡;你一定是最近才被感染的……

English: A word of advice. If you can find some way to rid yourself of it, do it quickly. Over the years it will merge with your flesh, until the mortal and the monster are one.
Chinese: 一句忠告。若你能找到什么办法摆脱它,尽快去做。年深日久,它会与你的血肉融合,直到凡人与怪物合为一体。

English: Look at me, young vierme - look at your wretched fate. You do not want this. ##Grow old, and happy, and die with pride.
Chinese: 看着我吧,年轻的维尔姆——看看你这可悲的命运。你不会想要这个的。##慢慢变老,快快乐乐,骄傲地死去。

English: Tell me about this parasite.
Chinese: 跟我讲讲这种寄生虫。

English: The vierme parasite is a long, serpent-like maggot. It festers in unseemly places and drops on its prey - quickly forcing itself inside their mouth.
Chinese: 维尔姆寄生虫是一条细长的、蛇形的蛆虫。它在阴暗不洁之处滋生,落在猎物身上——迅速钻进它们的嘴里。

English: It slithers down their throat and lodges in their bowels. Its toxins cloud their mind, veiling the latent horror with a false euphoria.
Chinese: 它滑入喉管,盘踞在肠腑之中。它的毒素迷障心智,用虚假的欣快遮蔽潜藏的恐怖。

English: The parasite cannot survive on normal food; it will force its host to choke it back up. Instead, in the dead of night, they crave the warmth of human skin. When the parasite feeds, it emerges from the host's mouth and uses its own teeth.
Chinese: 这种寄生虫无法靠寻常食物存活;它会逼迫宿主把食物吐出来。反之,在夜深人静之时,宿主会渴求人类肌肤的温暖。寄生虫进食时,会从宿主口中钻出,用自己的牙齿。

English: For the first century or so, the host appears not to age. But with time, the parasite merges with its host, until the two become one, and they look like... me.
Chinese: 头一百年左右,宿主看似不会衰老。但随着时间推移,寄生虫与宿主逐渐融合,直到二者合为一体,变成……我这副模样。

English: What sort of life have you led?
Chinese: 你过着怎样的生活?

English: I have lived for four hundred years; but I was not always the twisted vierme before you. Long ago I was a human girl, not so different from any other.
Chinese: 我活了四百年;但我并非生来就是你眼前这个扭曲的维尔姆。很久以前,我是一个人类女孩,与其他女孩并无不同。

English: Tell me about your 'youth'.
Chinese: 跟我讲讲你的"少年时代"。

English: As a girl I was called... Ezra Thornwood. I have not spoken that name for a long time.
Chinese: 当女孩时,我叫……艾兹拉·荆棘木。这个名字我已经很久没有说出口了。

English: My parents and I were refugees from the World Rend, if you can believe such a thing. We were lucky enough to be aboard an Emberian skyship which crashed on these isles. I was five years old.
Chinese: 我和父母是世界撕裂的难民,如果你能相信的话。我们幸运地搭上了一艘余烬飞船,它坠毁在这些岛屿上。那年我五岁。

English: Few remember it now, but Hallow Town started as a camp of those survivors. As a young girl, my parents gave me a harp and taught me the old Emberian songs. Beautiful stories of the great cities that I, nor anyone else, would ever see again.
Chinese: 如今鲜有人记得,但哈洛镇最初就是那些幸存者的营地。我还是小女孩时,父母送了我一架竖琴,教我古老的余烬歌谣。那些歌谣讲述着宏伟都市的美丽故事——无论我还是别的什么人,都再也见不到了。

English: It was in the woods that it... entered my throat. The parasite. I choked, retched - but to no avail. My parents would not consult the local Wikkans, as the Emberians were proud, secular folk. That night they found me feeding on my mother, the parasite half-emerged from my mouth.
Chinese: 就是在树林里,它……钻进了我的喉咙。寄生虫。我窒息,干呕——但无济于事。父母不肯去求助当地的维坎人,因为余烬人是骄傲的世俗之民。那天夜里,他们发现我正在啃食我的母亲,寄生虫半截探在我的嘴外。

English: I fled, and never saw my parents again.
Chinese: 我逃了,从此再没见过我的父母。

English: Tell me about your life as a vierme.
Chinese: 跟我讲讲你身为维尔姆的生活。

English: I travelled the skyrealms for a long time, moving from island to island. When I returned to my childhood home of Hallow Town I was more than a century old, though I looked not a day over twenty.
Chinese: 我在天空领域游荡了很久,辗转于各岛之间。当我回到童年的家哈洛镇时,我已年过百岁,看上去却不过二十。

English: Everyone I knew was dead. I remember sitting at the graves of my parents for days, trapped in a silent grief.
Chinese: 我认识的每一个人都死了。我记得在父母的墓前坐了好几天,困在无声的悲恸之中。

English: I found my old harp for sale - an antique. I bought it and played at the tavern, but everyone had forgotten the old songs. Folk followed the Wikkan ways; the Emberian cities had faded into myth.
Chinese: 我发现我那架旧竖琴在出售——成了古董。我买下它,在酒馆里弹奏,但所有人都忘了那些古老的歌谣。人们追随维坎之道;余烬的城市早已湮没为神话。

English: I doubt you can understand what it feels like to be a stranger in your own home. ##But I settled here, in Hallowshire. Made my fortune. Built this manor.
Chinese: 我怀疑你无法体会,在自己家中沦为异乡人是何种滋味。##但我还是在这里安顿下来,在哈洛郡。发了财。建起了这座庄园。

English: With time the parasite merged with my body. I was human no more; an elder vierme. ##It was harder to hide, and eventually, that damned kresnik found me here.
Chinese: 随着时间流逝,寄生虫与我的身体融为一体。我不再是人类;成了一位高龄维尔姆。##藏身变得越来越难,最终,那个该死的克雷斯尼克在这里找到了我。

English: Thank you for your story.
Chinese: 谢谢你讲的故事。

English: That's quite alright. If I am honest, I enjoyed telling it to someone. Thank you, for that.
Chinese: 不碍事。说实话,能讲给人听,我也很开心。为此谢谢你。

English: That's all I wanted to know.
Chinese: 我想了解的就这些了。

English: Very well.
Chinese: 很好。

English: How did you become imprisoned here?
Chinese: 你是怎么被囚禁在这里的?

English: You may have met the... ((caretaker)) that skulks on my grounds. Do not be fooled; that man is a [[kresnik]], a hunter of my kind.
Chinese: 你或许见过那个……在我地盘上鬼鬼祟祟的((管家)).别被蒙蔽;那人是[[克雷斯尼克]],专门猎杀我同类的人。

English: They claim to hunt parasites, but there is irony in that. For they do not kill their quarry but entrap them; bind them in their homes and live in their place.
Chinese: 他们号称猎杀寄生虫,其中却自有讽刺。因为他们并不杀死猎物,而是将其囚禁;把他们锁在自己的家中,取而代之住在里面。

English: It is more than simple theft. The kiss of a vierme is coveted by some. He comes to me, often enough - offering his flesh so this farce may continue.
Chinese: 这可不只是简单的偷窃。维尔姆之吻为某些人所觊觎。他时常来找我——献上他的血肉,好让这出闹剧继续演下去。

English: It has been fifty years now. First his father, who passed it to the son - they hunt in packs, you see. This infernal cipher seal prevents me from harming him, and the further I move from it the weaker I become. If I were to leave this island I would surely die.
Chinese: 至今已有五十年。起初是他的父亲,再传给儿子——你看,他们成群结队地狩猎。这可恶的密文封印使我无法伤害他,而我离它越远就越虚弱。若我离开这座岛,必死无疑。

English: That infernal cipher seal prevented me from harming him, and the further I moved from it, the weaker I became. But with your help -after thirty years of entrapment - I am finally free.
Chinese: 那可恶的密文封印使我无法伤害他,而我离它越远就越虚弱。但多亏你的帮助——在被囚三十年之后——我终于自由了。

English: Farewell.
Chinese: 告辞。

English: <<You wake up breathless and drenched in sweat, your thoughts racing. You know where you must go.>>
Chinese: <<你从梦中惊醒,气喘吁吁,浑身是汗,思绪飞转。你知道自己必须去哪里。>>

English: <<You know from the vision; from flying over the [[Corrupted Lands]] with Vela. Past the [[abandoned diggers]], down to the very [[south-eastern tip]]; to the [[Lost City of Progress]]. ((That)) is where Horace's memories lie.>>
Chinese: <<你从幻象中知道;从与薇拉飞越[[腐化之地]]的那一幕。越过[[废弃的挖掘机]],一路向着[[东南角]];去往[[进步废都]].((那里))便是霍勒斯的记忆所在。>>

English: <<The man, dressed in elegant fineries, is grumbling over a weathered map .>> ##...This thing is more useless than a ((bloated god-corpse...))
Chinese: <<那男人衣着华丽,正对着一张磨损的地图嘟囔。>>##……这东西比一具((胀气的神尸))还没用……

English: <<Suddenly he notices you.>> Ah! You there! Perchance could you help a ((humble)) merchant in his time of need, eh?
Chinese: <<他突然注意到你。>>啊!那边那位!可否帮帮一位((卑微))商人渡过难关,嗯?

English: II have a sizeable delivery of Scryshroom Tea, bound for the Clockwork Kingdom. ##Now before you say it, I know, I know - the border crossing is [[locked up tight.]] But you see, I've been in contact with the only fellow around here who has an [[import permit]] for this bloody kingdom of cogs, or what-have-you.
Chinese: 我有一大批窥菇茶要送到发条王国。##你先别说,我知道,我知道——边境关卡[[锁得死死的]].但你看,我一直在联系这一带唯一有此齿轮王国[[进口许可证]]的家伙,诸如此类。

English: What was his name - M... Mika? Makka? Ah, it escapes me. ##But, the point is I can't bloody well ((find)) him, can I? This old map is all wrong!
Chinese: 他叫什么来着——米……米卡?马卡?啊,想不起来了。##但问题是,我他妈就是((找))不到他,对吧?这张旧地图全错了!

English: So, if you've seen the chap, will you let me know? There'll be coin in it for you.
Chinese: 所以,你要是见过那家伙,能告诉我吗?有硬币酬谢。

English: Mikhail? Yes, he's due south of here - along the cliffside.
Chinese: 米哈伊尔?对,他就在这里南边——沿着崖边。

English: Ah, my saviour! Fat lot of good this map did me, eh? They should get ((you)) to pen the bloody things.
Chinese: 啊,我的救星!这地图可真帮了大忙,嗯?真该让((你))来画这些破玩意。

English: As promised, here's some [[coin]] for your trouble - well earned, I must say.
Chinese: 说到做到,这是给你跑腿的[[硬币]]——受之无愧,我得说。

English: Now, since my assistant has left me in the lurch, I suppose I'll have to shift this cargo myself. <<He pauses.>> ## ...Ah, ((godsdamnit...))
Chinese: 好了,既然我的助手撂挑子了,看来这批货只能我自己搬了。<<他顿了顿。>>##……啊,((神啊……))

English: Sure, I'll let you know if I see him.
Chinese: 好的,我见到他会告诉你的。

English: <<He nods.>> You are most kind. In the meantime, I'll return to deciphering this ((blasted)) map...
Chinese: <<他点头。>>你真是太好了。在此期间,我继续破译这张((该死))的地图……

English: Hold on - do you think he can get ((people)) into the Kingdom?
Chinese: 等等——你觉得他能把((人))弄进王国吗?

English: <<The merchant frowns.>> Well, I dare say there isn't any ((other)) way to get into that blasted place - if you were desperate, it'd be worth a punt.
Chinese: <<商人皱眉。>>嗯,我敢说,要进那鬼地方也没有((别的))办法——你要是豁出去了,值得一试。

English: But why ((anyone)) would want to go there is beyond me. By all accounts, the King's policies have plunged the kingdom into turmoil. A loaf of bread is said to be worth more than a skyship! Why do you think I'm trying to flog this tea?
Chinese: 但((谁))会想去那种地方,我就搞不懂了。人人都说,国王的政策已把王国搅得天翻地覆。据说一个面包比一艘飞船还值钱!不然你以为我为什么拼命卖这茶?

English: Ahem. Anyhow, do let me know if you see him, won't you?
Chinese: 咳咳。总之,见到他记得告诉我,好吗?

English: I'm not some hired hand.
Chinese: 我可不是什么雇工。

English: <<He looks you up and down.>> Hmph. No, I ((suppose)) not. ##Well, good day to you.
Chinese: <<他上下打量你。>>哼。不,我想((确实))不是。##好吧,祝你愉快。

English: Ah, we meet again. I don't suppose you've caught sight of that fellow with an [[import permit to the Clockwork Kingdom]]?
Chinese: 啊,又见面了。你没碰见那个有[[发条王国进口许可证]]的家伙吧?

English: No, not yet.
Chinese: 还没。

English: <<He nods.>> I see, I see. Well, back to the map, I suppose. Maybe it's upside down...
Chinese: <<他点头。>>明白,明白。好吧,我想还是接着研究地图。也许它拿倒了……

English: Greetin's traveller. I'm sorry, but if you're a Clockwork citizen lookin' for refuge in the Apostatic Union, y'er gonna need an [[Apostatic Union Passport]] to cross this gatebridge.
Chinese: 你好啊,旅行者。抱歉,若你是发条王国的国民,想逃往叛教联盟避难,你需要一份[[叛教联盟护照]]才能过这座关卡桥。

English: Y'see, lots'a folk have been tryin' to flee the chaos of the Clockwork King, 'an this gatebridge 'as been designated to help Union folk - an' ((only)) Union folk - make the crossing. Nobles in Hallowshire reckon the place has enough problems without an influx of refugees.
Chinese: 你瞧,好多人都在逃离发条王的乱局,而这座关卡桥是专门帮联盟的人——((只有))联盟的人——过桥的。哈洛郡的贵族们认为,这地方没有难民涌入已经够多麻烦了。

English: Have you come from outside? It's not safe out there!
Chinese: 你是从外面来的吗?外面不安全!

English: There's...things out there, I saw them out my window. They were like...like...
Chinese: 外面有……东西,我从窗户看见它们了。它们就像……就像……

English: <<The woman gives a series of sputtering, rattling coughs. >>##Augh...I'd stay back, if I was you. I'm...##<<The rest of her words are unintelligible, lost again in a spasm of coughs.>>
Chinese: <<那女人发出一连串噼啪作响的咳嗽。>>##呃啊……我要是你,就离远点。我……##<<她接下来的话含混不清,又淹没在一阵咳嗽里。>>

English: It's so clear out here! So clean!##You...you were the one who came from outside...did you do this?
Chinese: 外面这么明朗!这么干净!##你……你是从外面来的那个……是你干的吗?

English: Thank you, then! A thousand thank yous!##Here, take this.
Chinese: 那真是太感谢了!千恩万谢!##给,收下这个。

English: But, if you don't mind my asking.. how did you do it?
Chinese: 不过,恕我冒昧……你是怎么做到的?

English: <<Her bright face falters as you unfold your tale.>>##I...I cannot say I am not grateful, but you'll excuse me if...that is... Leave us, please! You've...you've done enough!
Chinese: <<你讲述经过时,她明朗的脸色黯淡下来。>>##我……我不能说我不感激,但请原谅我……就是说……请离开吧!你……你做得够多了!

English: Leave us, please! You've...you've done enough!
Chinese: 请离开吧!你……你做得够多了!

English: <<She looks at you bright-eyed.>>##Thank you so much. For everything.
Chinese: <<她目光清亮地看着你。>>##太感谢你了。感谢一切。

English: Just happy to be of service.
Chinese: 能帮上忙就好。

English: <<Do not answer>>
Chinese: <<不作回答>>

English: <<Tell her what you've done.>>
Chinese: <<告诉她你做了什么。>>

English: <<Leave out the dark parts>>
Chinese: <<略去黑暗的部分>>

English: Hm, what's this? ((Another)) would-be adventurer on this drifting rock? I dare say, it's getting crowded here.
Chinese: 嗯,这是什么?这座漂流岩上((又))来了一位准冒险家?我看,这里越来越挤了。

English: So, out with it, then - are you ((also)) seeking the [[treasure]] that lies behind that stone door?
Chinese: 那么,直说吧——你((也))在寻找那扇石门后的[[宝藏]]吗?

English: Uh, I guess so.
Chinese: 呃,大概是吧。

English: Well, this just can't do! We can't ((both)) claim ownership of whatever lies beyond that door - imagine the embarrassment of admitting to the Riovan Spelunker's Guild that you had ((help!))
Chinese: 哎,这可不行!门后无论是什么,我们不能((俩人))都认领——想想看,要是向里奥瓦洞穴探险家协会承认你((有帮手)),多难为情!

English: Uh, I have no idea what you mean.
Chinese: 呃,我不明白你在说什么。

English: <<He squints.>> Hmm. Playing coy, are we? Well, let's assume you're telling the truth.
Chinese: <<他眯起眼。>>哼。装傻是吧?好吧,就当你说的属实。

English: I'll tell you what. If you help me get this door open - and stand aside when I lay claim to whatever waits within - I'll reward you ((handsomely)).
Chinese: 这样吧。你若帮我打开这扇门——在我认领门内之物时站到一边——我会((重重))酬谢你。

English: Nothing from this ancient cave, of course- but you can have something [[truly priceless]] from my merchant vessel in recompense.
Chinese: 这座古老洞穴里的东西自然归我——但作为报酬,你可以从我商船上挑一件[[真正的无价之宝]]。

English: All you have to do is [[pull this lever]] here, which will start some sort of timer. Then, you need to find [[ten secret switches]] that will unlock the door mechanism, before the [[time runs out]].
Chinese: 你要做的就是[[拉下这根拉杆]],它会启动某种计时器。然后,你需要在[[时间耗尽]]之前找到[[十个秘密开关]],以解锁门的机关。

English: Only, a catch: it seems as though the [[switches]] were themselves quite valuable, and have been plundered by the locals. For all we know, they could be [[scattered all over the Oneiric Isles.]]
Chinese: 只是有个麻烦:那些[[开关]]本身似乎也相当值钱,已经被当地人搜刮走了。谁知道呢,它们可能[[散落在梦幻群岛的各个角落]]。

English: Quite a conundrum, eh? But remember - if you manage to open that door, I'll make it worth your while, and then some.
Chinese: 相当棘手,对吧?但记住——你若真能打开那扇门,我不会亏待你,只多不少。

English: <<The adventurer yells furiously.>> ((Squidshit! Typhos-crap! Son of a silkslug! Confound it all!))
Chinese: <<冒险家怒吼。>>((乌贼屎!提福斯粪!丝蛞蝓养的!统统该死!))

English: Uh, are you okay?
Chinese: 呃,你还好吗?

English: What's the matter?
Chinese: 怎么回事?

English: The treasure! It's... it's...
Chinese: 宝藏!它是……它是……

English: ((It's a bloody I-O-U!))
Chinese: ((竟然是张该死的欠条!))

English: Look, this tablet here. In the prehistoric writings of the skydweller tribes, this roughly translates as...
Chinese: 看,这块石板。用天空部族的史前文字,这大致可以译为……

English: ((The great treasure hoard of...)) uh, I believe this translates as ((the Cloud Rider tribe))... ##((...has been loaned to our brethren of the Drifting Isles, for use of their... hot springs?))
Chinese: ((……大宝藏……))呃,我想这段译作((驭云部族))……##((……已借予漂流群岛的弟兄,以供其……温泉之用?))

English: ...the bastards ((gave it away!))
Chinese: ……那帮混蛋((把它送人了!))

English: <<He sighs.>> Well, you got the blasted thing open, so I suppose I should honour our deal.
Chinese: <<他叹息。>>好吧,你毕竟把那该死的门打开了,我想我应该履行我们的约定。

English: You may have my [[Adventurers' Cabin]], and all that lies within. I ordered my servants to dismantle it for transport.
Chinese: 我的[[冒险家小屋]]和屋内的一切都归你了。我已吩咐仆人把它拆解以便搬运。

English: Now leave me. Perhaps there's still a gemstone left in the dirt, somewhere...
Chinese: 现在让我一个人静静。说不定这泥地里还剩一颗宝石,在某处……

English: I've been sent to keep track of this giant cephalok. It only turned up recently, and has some bigwigs in Hallowshire spooked.
Chinese: 我被派来追踪这头巨大的头颅兽。它是最近才出现的,把哈洛郡的一些大人物吓得不轻。

English: Apparently, legends tell of some wikkans who built a castle inside of a cephalok's shell - but, that sounds like nonsense to me. And what am I supposed to do, crawl inside of its throat?
Chinese: 据说,传说里有维坎人在头颅兽的壳里造了座城堡——但在我看来简直是胡说。再说我要干什么,爬进它的喉咙里去吗?
